correctness.rationale: The uniform inverse-branch weights give a triangular conditional update on the centered linear and quadratic observables, with linear multiplier sδ, quadratic multiplier b and cross coefficient −(1−d)/4. This forces the reverse-directed third moment to vanish and expresses the other as a sum of environment products. Odd products vanish by symmetry; the expectation of an even block is a product of independent adjacent-pair flip increments. This gives the all-lag formula, generating function and parity covariance. Grouping successive odd/even lags reduces the sign to the finite geometric series in z/b²; zeros occur precisely in the stated two classes at the boundary. The identity b²/d=(1/d+6+9d)/16 has unique minimum 3/4 at d=1/3, giving p=1/8 as the sharp envelope; for p<1/8 both root endpoints are inside (0,1). The other algebraic discriminant zero, p=1/2, has no admissible double root in d. Strict asymmetry already at lag one proves nonreversibility everywhere in the stated domain.
residual_risks: The sign threshold is annealed. At p<1/8, δ must still lie inside the claimed window for any positive lag. It is not a statement for arbitrary switching environments, observables or parameters at the excluded endpoints.

value.rationale: For a natural stationary full-branch benchmark with reversible switching, the observed spatial law is already irreversible at lag one while higher-lag directional moments cross a sharp explicit boundary. The all-lag calculation identifies exactly when and at which residue classes a sign-based diagnostic would change its conclusion about direction; the simultaneous covariance law distinguishes that information from second-order correlation. The threshold is in switching persistence, not an arbitrary slice or an onset of irreversibility.
residual_risks: The sign diagram is for one observable and one symmetric complementary environmental model; it does not characterize reversal statistics for general random maps.
